name: Ittai
bio: Ittai the Gittite was a foreign-born commander, a recent exile from Gath who had already thrown in his lot with David when Absalom's rebellion forced the king to flee Jerusalem. As David's household and six hundred Gittite loyalists passed by, David urged Ittai to turn back rather than share in his uncertain fate, since he was a newcomer and an exile with no obligation to David at all. Ittai refused, answering with an oath of loyalty that echoes Ruth's famous vow: "As surely as the LORD lives, and as my lord the king lives, wherever my lord the king may be, whether it means life or death, there will your servant be" (2 Samuel 15:19-21). David accepted him, and Ittai crossed the Kidron Valley with his men and all their little ones, among the few who stayed unwaveringly at David's side in his darkest hour (2 Samuel 15:22). Ittai's command of a third of David's army during the decisive battle against Absalom is told in detail in the chapters ahead.
